walkthroughs.body_html: Old Major's speech in Chapter 1 calls humans tyrants and dreams of an animal society. After his death, the pigs - Napoleon, Snowball, and Squealer - lead the rebellion against the drunken farmer Mr Jones. Manor Farm is renamed Animal Farm and the Seven Commandments are painted on the barn.

Boxer the carthorse and Clover stand for the working class; Benjamin the donkey is cynical and silent; Mollie the vain mare flees to humans; the sheep bleat slogans; the dogs become enforcers. Each animal speaks for a class, an attitude or a tool of power.

Orwell was a democratic socialist who fought in the Spanish Civil War and despised Stalin's betrayal of revolution. Animal Farm, finished in 1944, was his warning that totalitarianism corrupts even the noblest causes. He had trouble finding a publisher because Britain was still allied with the USSR.
